text:
incident-bot: P1 page triggered — unusual inter-region routing pattern detected affecting eu-west and apac endpoints. Observability alert: elevated 5xx + increased tail latency. Automated runbooks engaged :rotating_light:

alice-oncall: seeing 10-15% error spike for /v1/generate in eu-west, customers reporting timeouts. dashboard: https://console.redwood/intern/alerts/1751004321 

ben-sre: I can see broad DNS fanout to an unexpected upstream ASN from our egress fabric. Some queries are traversing ASN 64599 instead of expected partner ASN 64444. suspect BGP path change at edge. grabbing traceroutes. :eyes:

ben-sre: traceroute eu-west-router ->
```
traceroute to eu-west-api.redwood (34.78.21.11), 30 hops max
 1  10.128.0.1
 2  203.0.113.1
 3  * * *
 4  198.51.100.2  24.3 ms  23.8 ms  24.0 ms
 5  203.0.114.5  AS64599  60.1 ms  59.8 ms  60.2 ms
```
\ncarla-product: customer-impact table shows 12 paid customers with severe errors (20%+ request failures) and broader SLO alerts. Are we able to do a temporary regional pin to keep eu traffic in-region?

dave-netops: DNS traces show some negative caching events — a stale NXDOMAIN from an edge resolver got propagated then cached by downstream resolvers (TTL 300 but cached with negative cache behavior). That created a window where routing fell back to alternate regions. We'll need to flush our edge resolver caches and push a corrective BGP community with more-specific path to prefer 64444.

elaine-engr: I can push a short-term workaround: apply per-region routing override to force eu-west -> eu-west pool (pin) via control-plane with 5m TTL and increase retries on client side. Doing a small canary to 5% first.

ben-sre: rolling cache flush now on edge resolvers in eu-west (cmd: rdns flush --region eu-west --edge all). kicking off flush job.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: control-plane change submitted by elaine-engr — routing override canary (5% eu-west pinned) — runbook: https://playbooks/redwood/routing/edge-cache-flush.md

alice-oncall: canary looks good so far (5%): error rate down from 18% -> 6% in the canary cohort. expanding to 25%. notifying CS. :thumbsup:

dave-netops: BGP provider confirms an upstream path rehome that started at 09:12 UTC — unhappy notifier from ASN 64599 had a propagated more-specific that affected some egress POPs. They've withdrawn the route and we see AS64444 preferred now. Waiting for global BGP convergence.

ben-sre: all-edge caches flushed completed 09:28 UTC. negative cache entries cleared. monitoring for reappearance.

carla-product: notifying impacted customers via status page with ETA and mitigation steps. Draft posted: "We detected intermittent errors for EU/APAC regions caused by transient edge routing and DNS caching. A fix is rolling out; we expect normal traffic in 15-30 minutes."

elaine-engr: expanding pin to 100% on eu-west (control-plane change applied). keeping apac read-only pin in place while we verify no regressions.

alice-oncall: metrics confirm eu-west 5xx back to baseline and p95 latency normalizing. apac still has small tail, looks like a different POP affected — ben, can you trace apac?

ben-sre: APAC traces show similar pattern but limited to a single transit peer in ap-southeast. I've opened an ops ticket with transit vendor and applied local pin for ap-southeast POP.

sre-lead: good coordination. next steps: (1) keep routing override in place for 1 hour, (2) validate no further negative caching, (3) vendor postmortem requested for ASN path change, (4) follow up incident writeup. handing to oncall-night @alice-oncall for watch.

alice-oncall: ack handoff. I'll keep monitoring and escalate if error rate creeps above 5%. linking incident timeline: https://incidents.redwood/1751004321/timeline

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitor. P1 -> downgraded to P2 for follow-up.
